text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in nine straight games, 16 goals in all, with a point in eleven straight, and the reason to take it seriously is that the chances came with it. Over his last ten games he has 6.2 expected goals on his own shots against 4.7 at his usual rate (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and his ice time is up 1:36 a night. That is a player getting to better places more often, not just a hot stick. Beckett Sennecke has 17 points in his last ten beside him, though our numbers flag him as due to cool. Anaheim opens a four-game road trip here at 23 points, with a 63% playoff chance in our simulations.

St. Louis has a homecoming. Mason McTavish faces the Ducks for the first time since leaving them after 304 games in their colors. The other story in St. Louis is in net. Jordan Binnington has spent two weeks in trade-rumor headlines, from the Oilers to the Rangers, while Joel Hofer took 15 of the 20 starts, including a 1-0 win over Utah settled in an eight-round shootout. Tonight Binnington gets the start, at .849 and minus-3.5 goals saved above expected in five games after a minus-22.9 season last year. Every start now doubles as an audition, whoever is watching. Logan Mailloux is back from injured reserve, and the Blues are without Ross Johnston (upper body) and Dillon Dube.

Anaheim counters with Ville Husso, .881 and about even with his chances in seven games. The Ducks play without Ryan Poehling (knee) and A.J. Greer; Leo Carlsson has moved into Poehling's spot beside Nesterenko and Killorn. Their habit to watch is discipline: 4.8 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents the puck on the power play. Our depth sleeper is Jeff Malott, a fourth-liner whose last ten games produced 2.3 expected goals.

Our numbers have this one tight: 3.30 expected goals for Anaheim, 3.20 for St. Louis.
headline: Gauthier's streak meets McTavish's homecoming
